Title: Diagnosis
Details: The test case `testTrivial()` in `NonLinearConjugateGradientOptimizerTest` failed because the optimizer did not properly increment its iteration count, causing the `getIterations()` method to return zero. The current bug report highlights a similar issue with `LevenbergMarquardtOptimizer` not updating iterations correctly. 

Inspection of the base class `BaseOptimizer` shows the `getIterations()` method returns the count from an `Incrementor` object tracking iterations, which is initialized and reset properly in `optimize()`. The core optimization logic happens in `doOptimize()`, specifically in `NonLinearConjugateGradientOptimizer.doOptimize()`. The iteration is managed locally by a variable `iter` which increments on each loop but does not call any method in `BaseOptimizer` to update the shared iteration count stored in `iterations`. 

Further, the `BaseOptimizer` class provides a protected method `incrementIterationsCounter()` to increment the iterations `Incrementor`, but this method is never called within `NonLinearConjugateGradientOptimizer.doOptimize()`, meaning the global iteration tracking state remains at zero.

Hence, the root problem is that the subclass optimizer does not synchronize its local iteration variable (`iter`) with the base class incrementor `iterations`. It fails to invoke `incrementIterationsCounter()` in each iteration loop, so `getIterations()` reports zero even after performing iterations.

This diagnosis aligns with the symptoms in the failing test and the current bug report indicating missing iteration count updates. The missing call to increment the iteration counter within the optimization iteration loop is the cause of the bug.

Next steps would involve fixing the `NonLinearConjugateGradientOptimizer.doOptimize()` method to increment the iteration count using `incrementIterationsCounter()` on each iteration loop.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
